key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and they can be rapidly detected with reflected-light microscopy plus machine learning.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, non-invasive pre-screening of perovskite solar-cell films to flag stability risks before device integration and scale-up.
method: Chemically validate impurities with nano-FTIR and high-resolution optical/scanning-probe imaging
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation initiation at impurity-perovskite interfaces
Train image-analysis workflows on reflected-light microscopy for seconds-level impurity detection
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that films with higher impurity density degraded faster at early times, and degradation tracking indicated coupled photo- and thermo-chemical instability.
watch_item: Performance depends on robust image-quality and model calibration across film compositions, processing routes, and microscope setups.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
